title: Calcium stores, corrected calcium and intestinal absorption
guide: Total 1000–1300 g: 99.3% bone, 0.6% soft tissue (48% ionized, 40% albumin, 12% other), 0.1% ECF. Corrected Ca 8.6–10.3; formula +0.8(4−albumin); <8.4 hypo, >10.5 hyper. Ionized Ca: CaSR sensitisation, myocyte contractility, neuromuscular activity, bone mineralization; acidosis ↑ free Ca (0.1 pH → 0.1 meq/L). Absorption jejunum > duodenum, 20% net (~200 mg), acid enhances; 95% transcellular calcitriol-controlled (nuclear receptor → calbindin → TRPV5/6 → Ca-ATPase), 5% paracellular independent.

title: Urinary thresholds, milk-alkali syndrome and renal calcium handling
guide: ~200 mg/day urinary loss; 4 mg/kg/24 h; stones '4/7/11': hypercalciuria >4 (m/c), hyperuricosuria >7 (2nd), hypocitraturia <11. Milk-alkali: >4 g/day intake → paracellular entry → hypercalciuria/stones + hypercalcaemia → CaSR → ↓absorption & ↓ADH → volume depletion → RAAS → metabolic alkalosis. Renal: PCT 65% paracellular independent; TAL 25% dependent; DCT 10% active most dependent. ↑Ionized Ca: seconds → parathyroid CaSR ↓PTH (immediate); days → TAL CaSR ↓reabsorption → hypercalciuria (delayed). TAL CLDN16/19 + claudin-14.

title: Half-lives and CaSR mutation disorders
guide: Half-lives PTH 2–4 min, calcitriol 6–8 h, 25(OH)D3 2–3 wks (assay form). Gain-of-function CaSR = Bartter type V (AD; others AR): ↑↑↑ excretion → hypocalcaemia (others hypercalcaemia). Loss-of-function = FHH (children, AD): no excretion → complete reabsorption → hypocalciuria + hypercalcaemia.
